slides.title: Abstract Classes

blocks.text: With inheritance, classes become more specific with each new subclass.
If you move up from a subclass to a superclass, the superclass becomes more general and less specific.
Class design should ensure that a superclass contains common features of its subclasses.
Such a superclass is referred to an abstract class. It cannot be used to create any specific instance.

slides.title: Abstract Methods

blocks.text: We previously defined GeometricObject as the superclass
of Circle and Rectangle.
Both Circle and Rectangle contain the getArea and getPerimeter methods for a circle and rectangle object.
Since the area and perimeter can be computed for all geometric objects, we can define the getArea and getPerimeter methods in the GeometricObject class.
However, these two methods cannot be implemented in
GeometricObject and are referred to as abstract methods.

slides.title: Abstract Method in Abstract Class

blocks.text: An abstract method must be defined in an abstract class.
A non-abstract class is called a concrete class.
A concrete subclass of an abstract superclass must implement all the abstract methods of the superclass.
The Circle and Rectangle subclasses implement the getArea and getPerimeter abstract methods.
If a subclass of an abstract superclass does not implement all the abstract methods, the subclass must be defined abstract.

slides.title: Cannot Instantiate an Abstract Class

blocks.text: Objects cannot be created from an abstract class.
Cannot use the new operator to instantiate an abstract class.
However, you can still define the constructors of an abstract class, which are invoked in the constructors of its subclasses.
For instance, the constructors of GeometricObject are invoked in the Circle and the Rectangle subclasses.

slides.title: Notes about Abstract Classes

blocks.text: It is possible to define an abstract class without any abstract method. The abstract class is used as a base for subclasses.
A subclass can be abstract even if its superclass is concrete.
For example, the root class Object class is concrete, but a subclass, such as GeometricObject, is abstract.
An abstract class can be used as a data type. For example, but you can create an array of GeometricObject elements.

slides.title: The Abstract Calendar Class

blocks.text: An instance of java.util.Date represents a specific instant in time with a long millisecond precision.
The java.util.Calendar is an abstract base class for extracting detailed information such as year, month, day, hour, minute and second from a Date object.
Subclasses of Calendar can implement specific calendar systems such as the Gregorian or lunar calendar.
The java.util.GregorianCalendar is supported in the
Java API for the Gregorian calendar.

slides.title: The Concrete Gregorian Calendar Class

blocks.text: Use new GregorianCalendar() to construct a default
GregorianCalendar object for the current time.
Use new GregorianCalendar(year, month, day) to construct a GregorianCalendar object for the specified year, month, and day.
The month parameter is 0-based, where 0 is for January.
Use new GregorianCalendar(year, month, day, hour, minute, second) to construct an object for the specified year, month, day, hour, minute, and second.
